subject: Urgent: sustained latency spikes and elevated 500s — Glyph Health
messages:
From: Lena Park <lena.park@glyphhealth.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 09 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sustained latency spikes & 500s — urgent

Stephanie —

We started seeing large latency spikes and intermittent 500 errors on our production inference endpoints starting ~08:45 PDT. The errors coincide with a burst of traffic from our triage pipeline; p50 looks fine but p95/p99 and error rate ramp up quickly. We've attached a short metrics dump and a few traces.

Impact: multiple customer-facing request timeouts and two workflows failed end-to-end. This is affecting the contract SLA. Can your team confirm whether this is a config change on your side or something in our prompts/model? We need a mitigation plan and an ETA.

Attachments: glyph_latency_metrics_0909.csv, glyph_traces_0909.zip

Lena Park
Head of Platform Reliability
Glyph Health
From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Lena Park <lena.park@glyphhealth.com>
Cc: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 09 Sep 2028 09:20:13 -0700
Subject: Re: Sustained latency spikes & 500s — urgent

Thanks Lena — we see the alert and are investigating. I'm opening an incident (INF-9391) and looping in infra/ops. First steps: collect KV-cache metrics, prefix/routing heatmaps, and tracer spans. Can you confirm whether you were running any new integration jobs or significant traffic bursts at 08:40–09:00?

We will provide a short mitigation (possible rollback of recent cache tuning) within 30 minutes. I will keep you updated every 30 minutes until it's resolved.

-Stephanie
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 09 Sep 2028 09:35:55 -0700
Subject: Re: Sustained latency spikes & 500s — urgent

I'm attaching an initial kv-dump and the KV hot-lane metrics for the affected pool. Early signs point at a sudden working set shift where many mid-cardinality prefixes became hot simultaneously, triggering aggressive prefetch and eviction churn. Two things stand out: TTLs for prefix-level entries were shortened in the last rollout (to reduce memory pressure) and the hot-lane slot count was reduced for cost smoothing. That combination can cause cache respawn: lots of simultaneous misses -> prefetch storms -> HOL blocking on hot-shards.

Immediate suggestion: roll back TTL change to previous profile and temporarily restore hot-lane capacity for the affected pool to absorb the working set. We'll canary the change on 1% of traffic first.

Attachment: kv-dump-step1.txt

Jonas Weber
Senior SRE, Inference Runtime
From: naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 09 Sep 2028 10:02:07 -0700
Subject: Re: Sustained latency spikes & 500s — urgent

Executed a targeted canary: increased hot-lane slots x3 and reverted prefix-TTL for pool glyph-prod-1 on two hosts. Short-term: p50 improved but p99 and error rate rose on the baseline hosts that we didn't touch — looks like HOL blocking propagated because those hosts saw a sudden influx of evicted prefixes trying to prefetch and saturating their prefetch queues.

We are pausing further rollout and preparing a full rollback of the prior tuning set to the previous stable profile. If we roll back across the fleet it should restore previous steady-state behavior within ~8–12 minutes after caches warm.

Naomi
Tech Ops Engineer
From: Aaron Liu <aaron.liu@glyphhealth.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Lena Park <lena.park@glyphhealth.com>
Date: Sat, 09 Sep 2028 11:18:29 -0700
Subject: Re: Sustained latency spikes & 500s — urgent

Thanks. The errors have continued in waves; visibility shows timeouts at the application layer and 502/500 spikes in our logs. Our legal/finance team is asking for an SLA impact estimate and whether we should expect credits. Please escalate to leadership — this is impacting a go-live for a key customer.

Aaron Liu
Platform Engineer
Glyph Health
From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 09 Sep 2028 11:42:10 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Sustained latency spikes & 500s — leadership escalation requested

Marissa — looping you in. Glyph is seeing persistent p99 latency spikes and intermittent 500s during a burst that started this morning. Root cause looks like a cache-respawn / prefetch storm triggered by our recent prefix-TTL and hot-lane reduction. Naomi's rollback plan is ready; Jonas recommends fleet rollback to the previous cache profile and a phased re-introduction of hot-lane capacity.

Short asks for leadership:
- Approve fleet rollback to stable cache profile (low-risk; expected recovery 8–12 minutes after changes)
- Approve a 1-week temporary increase in hot-lane capacity for Glyph's reservation pool while we retune heuristics (estimated incremental cost ~$6k)
- Approve an immediate courtesy credit (suggest 10%) and a joint postmortem within 3 business days

I'll initiate the rollback once you OK.

-Stephanie
From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 09 Sep 2028 13:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sustained latency spikes & 500s — leadership escalation requested

Plan update and timeline:
- Rolling back cache TTL/hot-lane profile across the fleet starting 12:00 UTC (will perform a canary at 1% then 10% before full rollout).
- Expect visible recovery within two prefetch cycles (~8–12 minutes) after full rollback.
- We're instrumenting additional prefetch backpressure and a short-term safeguard: prefetch queue depth limit and a conservative retry backoff to avoid respawn storms.

Attachments: postmortem-draft.md
Jira: INF-9391

If approved, step will begin immediately after Marissa's OK.

Jonas
